grid.note: wavelength = center_nm[frame][ring] + offset_nm. declared_line: the window is centred on the ring's own (declared) laser line, so offset = wavelength minus line. resonance: centred on the ring's resonance of the order nearest its declared line (the cold start, where the resonance starts nm away from any line)

bus.note: the engine's own optics outputs at t_s (Truth out_rl), [frame][ring][line] in mW: p_in = light of each line arriving at the ring's input after the bus segment (RL_PIN), p_thru = light of each line leaving its through port, data-averaged (RL_THRU); the bus between ring k and k+1 carries p_thru[k] going in and p_in[k+1] arriving (the difference is bus loss)

exact_note: resonance_level_nm [frame][ring][level]: the exact resonance of each NRZ level (order nearest the declared line); notch_level_db: the through transmission exactly there (the grid's 12.5 pm step does not resolve the bottom of a deep notch; draw the bottom from these)
note: power transmission of each ring alone (input 1 W on the bus at that wavelength): thru0_db / thru1_db the through port with the junction at NRZ level 0 (v_lo, lower reverse bias) / level 1 (v_hi); drop_db the drop port (to the monitor PD) averaged over the data, ones_density x level 1 + (1 - ones_density) x level 0, which is what the monitor and the lock see. The NRZ-averaged through port is the same average of thru0 and thru1 in linear units. Computed with the model's phase model (mrm.plant.phase) and exact ring (mrm.plant.optics.ring_exact) at the ring's state at t_s (ring and heater-resistor temperature, bias levels): rigid-comb phase model, no backscatter (g26).
